title: Brick Wall
summary: Given a rectangular brick wall with n rows, where each row contains bricks of varying widths but the total width of each row is the same, determine the minimum number of bricks that a vertical line drawn from the top to the bottom will cross.
statement: Given a rectangular brick wall with n rows, where each row contains bricks of varying widths but the total width of each row is the same, determine the minimum number of bricks that a vertical line drawn from the top to the bottom will cross. The line should not pass through the vertical edges of the wall, and if it passes through the edge of a brick, the brick is not considered crossed.
constraints: Each row has equal total width. A line through an internal edge crosses no brick; it may not use either outer wall edge.
hints: Safe cuts occur at cumulative internal widths.
Choose the internal edge shared by the most rows.
Count each row prefix except its full width; return rows minus best count.
The line crosses exactly rows that lack its position as an internal brick boundary.
editorial: The line crosses exactly rows that lack its position as an internal brick boundary.

tests.explanation: Four rows share an internal edge, so six minus four equals two crossed bricks.
There are no internal edges to use, so every one of three bricks is crossed.
